title: General comments about the use of CASCADE
text:
Pre-requisites

A file (.mzML) containing DDA MS data with an additional detector (PDA, ELSD, CAD)
A file (.csv) containing features, as obtained by mzmine
A file (.tsv) containing annotations, as obtained by TIMA

All coming steps admit you already installed cascade:

install.packages(
  "cascade",
  repos = c(
    "https://adafede.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cran.r-universe.dev",
    "https://bioc.r-universe.dev"
  )
)

section: Check the raw data and alignment
text:
Check the raw data and alignment
First, check if the raw data can be aligned to your expectations:

check_chromatograms_alignment(show_example = TRUE)





Or, with more details:

check_chromatograms_alignment(
  show_example = TRUE,
  time_min = 0.5,
  time_max = 35.0,
  type = "improved",
  chromatograms = c(
    "bpi_pos",
    "cad_pos",
    "pda_pos",
    "bpi_neg",
    "cad_neg",
    "pda_neg"
  )
)





How it should not look like (CAD and PDA shifts incorrectly set):

check_chromatograms_alignment(
  show_example = TRUE,
  time_min = 0.5,
  time_max = 35.0,
  cad_shift = 1,
  pda_shift = 2,
  type = "baselined",
  chromatograms = c(
    "bpi_pos",
    "cad_pos",
    "pda_pos"
  )
)

title: cascade
text:
Architecture & Performance Overhaul

Reduced external package dependencies from 17 to 7 (baseline, curl, data.table, ggplot2, gt, mzR, plotly), removing BiocParallel, caTools, forcats, htmltools, httr2, MSnbase, purrr, R.utils, tidytable, and tima.
Consolidated 66 fragmented R/*.R files into 20 cohesive modules with explicit Collate ordering and full Roxygen2 documentation.
Rewrote all tabular pipelines in idiomatic data.table (fread(), fwrite(), foverlaps(), rbindlist(), melt(), dcast()) and base R vectorization.
Replaced MSnbase::chromatogram() with a vectorized S4 MS1 scan extractor (extract_ms_peak(), extract_ms_progress()) that parses and binary-searches MS1 scans across all features simultaneously.
Replaced caTools::runmean() with a fast base-R centered moving average (runmean_center()) and MSnbase::closest() with a vectorized binary-search matcher (closest_idx()).

title: cascade
text:
Completed In-Progress Functions & Palettes

Acetonitrile gradient response correction (p_acn_i(), predict_response()): Vectorized both functions in R/annotations.R and wired them into prepare_comparison() and generate_pseudochromatograms() via correct_acn = FALSE, acn_time = 30.5, and dvol = 0.5.
Signal-based sunburst plots (plot_results_2()): Completed in R/hierarchy.R using data.table and wired into generate_pseudochromatograms(), returning plots_2 (sunburst_signal_based_duo and sunburst_conf_signal_based_duo) alongside plots_1 and treemaps.
Interactive Wikidata/LOTUS gt tables (format_gt()): Completed in R/query_wikidata.R without requiring htmltools and wired into generate_ids() via format_tables = FALSE (returning tables alongside plots, treemaps, and sunbursts).
Titled treemaps and sunbursts (treemaps_progress()): Completed in R/hierarchy.R with explicit tables argument passing to display unique structure counts in plot titles, and wired into generate_ids() via show_title = FALSE.
Color palettes (R/colors.R): Preserved all qualitative and sequential color palettes (microshades, microshades_grey, microshades_colors, paired, minibits, tableau20, discrete_rainbow_14, discrete_rainbow_23, elife, green_4, blue_4, pink_4, green_24, blue_24, pink_24) and bundled them into cascade_palettes.

title: cascade
text:
Retired Prototype Functions

plot_histograms(): Superseded by plot_histograms_confident() and plot_histograms_taxo() (for continuous retention-time pseudochromatograms) and plot_histograms_litt() (for discrete taxon/sample stacked bar charts).
plot_chromatogram(): Unused 15-line plotly scratch wrapper expecting a non-standard time column (cascade uses rtime); superseded by check_chromatograms_alignment() and plot_peak_detection().
prehistograms_progress() and histograms_progress(): Trivial 1-line map() wrappers around prepare_plot() and plot_histograms(), replaced by direct lapply() calls in generate_ids() and plot_tima().
save_histograms_progress() and save_treemaps_progress(): Referenced external global pipeline variables (paths, dimensions, size) not present in the package and relied on deprecated plotly::save_image().

text:
Performs a SPARQL query against Wikidata (or another SPARQL 1.1 endpoint) and returns a data.table. Requests gzip-compressed CSV (falling back to TSV) streamed directly to disk via curl and parsed with data.table::fread(). Automatically retries against the QLever Wikidata endpoint (https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata) when fallback = TRUE.



query_wikidata(
  sparql_query,
  remove_url = TRUE,
  endpoint = "https://query.wikidata.org/sparql",
  agent = "https://github.com/adafede/cascade",
  timeout = 3600L,
  fallback = TRUE,
  headers = NULL,
  post = FALSE
)







sparql_query


Character(1). SPARQL query string.




remove_url


Logical(1). Strip http(s)://www.wikidata.org/entity/ prefix from character columns (default TRUE).




endpoint


Character(1). SPARQL endpoint URL. Default is “https://query.wikidata.org/sparql”.




agent


Character(1). HTTP User-Agent header string.




timeout


Numeric(1). Total request timeout in seconds (default 3600L).




fallback


Logical(1). Retry with QLever Wikidata endpoint on failure (default TRUE).




headers


Character(1) or NULL. Optional Accept header for backward compatibility.




post


Logical(1). Send the SPARQL query as an HTTP POST request body (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) rather than a GET query parameter (default FALSE).






A data.table containing the query results.




library("cascade")


q <- "SELECT ?taxon WHERE { ?taxon <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/P225> 'Gentiana lutea' . }"
try(query_wikidata(q, timeout = 15L))

     taxon
    <char>
1: Q158572

text:
Extracts MS1 ion chromatograms (XICs) for all features falling within detected chromatographic peaks (e.g., CAD, PDA, or BPI), computes Pearson correlation similarity scores between each feature’s XIC profile and the corresponding detector peak profile, and exports both peak-informed and non-informed feature tables as TSV files.



process_compare_peaks(
  file = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  type = "baselined",
  detector = "cad",
  headers = c(bpi = "BasePeak_0", pda = "PDA#1_TotalAbsorbance_0", cad = "UV#1_CAD_1_0"),
  export_dir = "data/interim/peaks",
  show_example = FALSE,
  fourier_components = 0.01,
  frequency = 1,
  min_area = 0.005,
  min_intensity = 10000,
  resample = 1,
  shift = 0.05,
  time_min = 0.5,
  time_max = 32.5
)







file


Path to .mzML file (optional when show_example = TRUE).




features


Path to feature table (optional when show_example = TRUE).




type


Chromatogram processing stage: “original”, “baselined”, or “improved”. Default is “baselined”.




detector


Detector type: “cad”, “bpi”, or “pda”. Default is “cad”.




headers


Named character vector mapping detector types to .mzML chromatogram header IDs.




export_dir


Directory where the output .tsv files are written. Default is “data/interim/peaks”.




show_example


Logical; use bundled example data. Default is FALSE.




fourier_components


Fraction of Fourier components to retain. Default is 0.01.




frequency


Acquisition frequency in Hz. Default is 1.




min_area


Minimum relative area fraction for peak filtering. Default is 0.005.




min_intensity


Minimum MS intensity for feature filtering. Default is 1e4.




resample


Resampling factor. Default is 1.




shift


Retention time shift in minutes. Default is 0.05.




time_min


Minimum retention time in minutes. Default is 0.5.




time_max


Maximum retention time in minutes. Default is 32.5.






Invisibly returns a named list with two data.table elements: features_informed and features_not_informed.




library("cascade")


tmp <- tempdir()
process_compare_peaks(show_example = TRUE, export_dir = tmp)

check_chromatograms_alignment(

  fourier_components = 0.01,
  frequency = 1,
  resample = 1,

  type = "baselined",
  normalize_intensity = TRUE,
  normalize_time = FALSE,
  show_example = FALSE,
  intensity_floor = 0.001,
  k2 = 250,
  k4 = 1250000,
  sigma = 0.05,
  smoothing_width = 8,
  baseline_method = "peakDetection",
  improve_signal = TRUE
)







file_negative


Path to negative-mode .mzML file (optional).




file_positive


Path to positive-mode .mzML file (optional).




time_min


Minimum retention time in minutes. Default is 0.5.




time_max


Maximum retention time in minutes. Default is 32.5.




cad_shift


CAD retention time shift in minutes. Default is 0.05.




pda_shift


PDA retention time shift in minutes. Default is 0.1.




fourier_components


Fraction of Fourier components to retain. Default is 0.01.




frequency


Acquisition frequency in Hz. Default is 1.




resample


Resampling factor. Default is 1.




chromatograms


Character vector of chromatograms to plot. Default is c(“bpi_pos”, “cad_pos”, “pda_pos”).




headers

type

Logical; normalize intensity to [0, 1]. Default is TRUE.




normalize_time


Logical; normalize time to [0, 1]. Default is FALSE.




show_example


Logical; use bundled example data. Default is FALSE.




intensity_floor


Small positive value for intensity floor. Default is 0.001.




k2


Second-derivative weight for signal sharpening. Default is 250.




k4


Fourth-derivative weight for signal sharpening. Default is 1250000.




sigma


Gaussian sigma for signal sharpening. Default is 0.05.




smoothing_width


Moving-average window width for derivative smoothing. Default is 8.




baseline_method


Baseline correction method passed to baseline::baseline(). Default is “peakDetection”.




improve_signal


Logical; apply Fourier filtering and sharpening. Default is TRUE.






A plotly htmlwidget displaying the aligned chromatograms.




library("cascade")

check_chromatograms_alignment(show_example = TRUE)

title: CASCADE
text:
Contextualizing untargeted Annotation with Semi-quantitative Charged Aerosol Detection for pertinent characterization of natural Extracts.
⚠️ This repository is not maintained and will not be except for extreme interest. It has just been opened for the sake of transparency.
The initial work is available at https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jafc.3c03099, with some improvements made since then. The workflow is illustrated below.




Here is what you minimally need:

A file (.mzML) containing DDA MS data with an additional detector (PDA, ELSD, CAD)

In case you don’t know how to obtain it, see: wiki/How-to-create-a-compliant-mzML-file

A file (.csv) containing features, as obtained by mzmine
A file (.tsv) containing annotations, as obtained by TIMA




As the package is not (yet) available on CRAN, you will need to install with:
install.packages(
  "cascade",
  repos = c(
    "https://adafede.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cran.r-universe.dev",
    "https://bioc.r-universe.dev"
  )
)
Once installed, you are ready to go through our documentation, with the major steps detailed.

Quick overview of the literature
To check (and eventually compare to your own results) what is known in the literature about different organisms:

bonus_plots_list <- generate_ids(
  taxa = c("Swertia", "Kopsia", "Ginkgo"),
  comparison = c("Swertia", "Kopsia"),
  no_stereo = TRUE,
  filter_ms_conditions = TRUE,
  start = "1950",
  end = "2025"
)


Compounds found in Swertia

Pseudo chromatograms
If you know want to add some cosmetics, and you already have a TIMA annotation table, you can then run:

plots_list <- generate_pseudochromatograms(show_example = TRUE)

The different plots offer the following views:
